2027-05-31.title: Third Monday of the Apostles · The Visitation of the Blessed Virgin Mary
2027-05-31.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
2027-05-31.alt: Season of the Apostles (Šleehe), which began at Pentecost: the Church remembers how the apostles, filled with the Holy Spirit, carried the Gospel to the nations. The Holy Qurbana is celebrated with the Anaphora of Addai and Mari, and from Pentecost the Angel of the Lord (Angelus) is prayed again in place of the Queen of Heaven. The Visitation of the Blessed Virgin Mary is listed in the First Set calendar as an important Marian feast, with the readings above. Weekday readings of the Third Monday of the Apostles: 1 Corinthians 12:18–27; John 6:30–36. The Latin Church keeps the feast of the Visitation on the same day. Today the month of Mary (May devotion) comes to its close in many parishes and homes (verify locally which readings are used).
2027-05-31.verse: And blessed is she who believed that there would be a fulfillment of what was spoken to her by the Lord.
theo: On the last day of the month of Mary the Church follows her on a journey. Luke has just told of the Annunciation: the angel has left, the Word has become flesh in her womb, and she has heard that her elderly kinswoman Elizabeth, who was called barren, is in her sixth month. Mary does not stay at home to guard her secret. “In those days Mary set out and went with haste to a Judean town in the hill country.” It was a long journey, perhaps four or five days on foot from Nazareth to the hill country of Judea, which tradition places at Ain Karem near Jerusalem. The haste is not anxiety; it is the haste of love and of joy. St Ambrose says that she went joyful in her desire, devout in her duty, eager in her gladness. The first thing Mary does after receiving Christ is to carry him to someone who needs her. That is the pattern of every Christian life, and especially of this Season of the Apostles: the one who has received Christ goes out in haste to bring him to others. Pope Francis took Mary's haste as the theme of the World Youth Day at Lisbon in 2023, “Mary arose and went with haste”, and told the young that it is the haste of one who cannot keep a great gift to herself.

Then the meeting: Mary “entered the house of Zechariah and greeted Elizabeth. When Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting, the child leaped in her womb. And Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit and exclaimed with a loud cry, ‘Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb. And why has this happened to me, that the mother of my Lord comes to me?’” Two women meet, one old and one young, both carrying a child that only God could give. But the real meeting is between the two children: John, still unborn, leaps for joy before the unborn Christ. The Church sees here John the Baptist filled with the Holy Spirit from his mother's womb, as the angel had promised (Luke 1:15). Elizabeth's words have become our own daily prayer: in every Hail Mary we say with her, “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb.” And she gives Mary the title that the Council of Ephesus would later solemnly proclaim: the mother of my Lord, the Mother of God.

Luke tells the story with words that recall the ark of the covenant. When King David brought the ark up to Jerusalem, he said, “How can the ark of the Lord come into my care?” (2 Samuel 6:9); he “danced before the Lord with all his might” (2 Samuel 6:14), and the ark remained three months in the house of Obed-edom, bringing blessing. Elizabeth asks, “why has this happened to me, that the mother of my Lord comes to me?” John leaps for joy, and Mary remains with Elizabeth about three months (Luke 1:56). The Fathers and many interpreters see the meaning: Mary is the new ark, carrying not tablets of stone but the living Word of God. The Syriac Fathers, St Ephrem among them, sing of her in images like these. St John Paul II added that at the Visitation Mary became in some way the first tabernacle in history; her journey has also been called the first Eucharistic procession. How fitting that this feast falls in the week of the Body and Blood of Christ, and that the weekday Gospel today has Jesus saying, “I am the bread of life” (John 6:35). Mary carried the Bread of Life to Elizabeth's house; we carry him from the altar into ours.

Elizabeth's last word is a beatitude, the first in Luke's Gospel: “And blessed is she who believed that there would be a fulfillment of what was spoken to her by the Lord.” Mary is blessed first not because of a privilege, but because she believed. She is the model of faith for every disciple. And from that faith comes love in action, which is what Paul describes in the Epistle chosen for the feast: “Let love be genuine; hate what is evil, hold fast to what is good; love one another with mutual affection; outdo one another in showing honor.” Then: “Contribute to the needs of the saints; extend hospitality to strangers… Rejoice with those who rejoice, weep with those who weep. Live in harmony with one another; do not be haughty, but associate with the lowly.” Every phrase could describe the three months at Ain Karem: a young woman who serves her older relative, rejoices with her, shares her house and her joys, and makes herself lowly though she carries the Lord. The weekday Epistle says the same in its own way: “If one member suffers, all suffer together with it; if one member is honored, all rejoice together with it” (1 Corinthians 12:26). As the month of Mary ends, the best homage we can give her is to do what she did: to believe the word of the Lord, and to set out in haste to serve someone who needs us.
conn: The ark comes to the hill country.

“How can the ark of the Lord come into my care?” (2 Samuel 6:9); David “danced before the Lord with all his might” (2 Samuel 6:14); the ark remained three months in the house of Obed-edom (2 Samuel 6:11).
“How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace” (Isaiah 52:7): Mary crosses the hills of Judea carrying the Prince of Peace.
Filled with the Spirit from the womb.
The angel had said of John: “even before his birth he will be filled with the Holy Spirit” (Luke 1:15).
Jael and Judith were called blessed among women for delivering Israel (Judges 5:24; Judith 13:18); Mary is blessed for the fruit of her womb, who delivers the world.
Mary answers Elizabeth with the Magnificat (Luke 1:46–55), echoing the song of Hannah (1 Samuel 2:1–10).
At the Cross Jesus gives his Mother to the beloved disciple: “Here is your mother” (John 19:27); the Church receives her into her own home.
altar: Mary carried the Lord in her womb to Elizabeth's house, and John leaped for joy. At the Holy Qurbana the same Lord comes to us under the forms of bread and wine; let our hearts leap like John's, and let us say with Elizabeth, “why has this happened to me, that my Lord comes to me?”
Receiving him, we become in our turn bearers of Christ. Like Mary, let us carry him in haste from the altar to those who wait for him.
outline: The last day of the month of Mary: a young woman on the road to the hill country.
Point 1 · She set out with haste
The first thing Mary does is to carry Christ to another.
Point 2 · The child leaped for joy
Two mothers, two children, and the Holy Spirit.
Point 3 · The mother of my Lord
Mary, the new ark and the first tabernacle.
Point 4 · Blessed is she who believed
An aunt from the hills arriving by bus with a bag of jackfruit chips and three months to give.
live: Visit this week someone who needs you: an expectant mother, an elderly relative, a sick neighbour. Do not postpone it.
Pray one decade of the Rosary today, pausing on Elizabeth's words in each Hail Mary.
Choose one promise of God that you find hard to believe, and repeat it in prayer each day this week.
Choose one phrase of today's Epistle and live it this week: hospitality, weeping with those who weep, or associating with the lowly.
fathers: Mary went with haste into the hill country, not as one who doubted the angel's word, but joyful in her desire, devout in her duty, eager in her gladness. The grace of the Holy Spirit knows no slow efforts. Elizabeth heard the voice first, but John felt the grace first.

Let the soul of Mary be in each of us to magnify the Lord; let the spirit of Mary be in each of us to rejoice in God. According to the flesh there is one mother of Christ, but according to faith Christ is the fruit of all who believe.

She who was raised by grace above all others remained humble. Mary does not glory in herself but in God her Saviour, and so teaches us that those who receive great gifts must give the more thanks and keep themselves the more lowly.
magis: Called in the Gospels the mother of Jesus, Mary is acclaimed by Elizabeth, at the prompting of the Spirit, even before the birth of her son, as the mother of my Lord; the Church confesses that Mary is truly Mother of God (Theotokos).
John the Baptist was filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother's womb; by the Spirit, Elizabeth was blessed with the visit of Mary.
The Virgin Mary most perfectly embodies the obedience of faith; that is why Elizabeth greets her: Blessed is she who believed.
The second part of the Hail Mary takes up Elizabeth's greeting: Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb.
St John Paul II, Ecclesia de Eucharistia 55
When, at the Visitation, Mary bore in her womb the Word made flesh, she became in some way a tabernacle, the first tabernacle in history.
saints: The Visitation of the Blessed Virgin Mary, an important Marian feast in the First Set calendar, kept on the same day in the Latin calendar. Close of the month of Mary.
Fri 4 June: the Sacred Heart of Jesus (Third Friday of the Apostles). Sun 6 June: Fourth Sunday of the Apostles.
2027-05-31.prayer: Lord God, you inspired the Blessed Virgin Mary, carrying your Son in her womb, to set out in haste to visit Elizabeth, and at her greeting John leaped for joy and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit. Give us Mary's faith, to believe that your word will be fulfilled, and her haste, to carry Christ to those who need him. Make our love genuine, our homes hospitable and our hearts lowly. As we close this month of Mary, keep us under her protection, and let us magnify you with her all our days. Through Christ our Lord, who lives and reigns with you and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.

quick: Mary sets out in haste to the hill country to visit Elizabeth.
At her greeting John leaps in the womb, and Elizabeth, filled with the Spirit, calls her the mother of my Lord.
Elizabeth: blessed is she who believed; Paul: let love be genuine, rejoice with those who rejoice, weep with those who weep.

2027-05-31.question: Whom is the Lord asking me to visit in haste?
catechism: Mother of my Lord: the Theotokos.
kidsaint: Elizabeth and her husband Zechariah were old and had no children. God gave them a baby, John. When Mary came to visit, baby John jumped for joy inside Elizabeth! Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit and said, “Blessed are you among women!” We say her words every time we pray the Hail Mary. Lesson: when Jesus comes close, our hearts can jump for joy too!
2027-05-31.special: Visitation of the Blessed Virgin Mary (important Marian feast). Close of the month of Mary.
term: The song of Mary in Luke 1:46–55, named from its first word in Latin: My soul magnifies the Lord. Mary sings it in the house of Elizabeth. The Church prays it every day, and it echoes the song of Hannah and the psalms of Israel: God lifts up the lowly and fills the hungry with good things.

family.explain: After the angel visited Mary, she heard that her cousin Elizabeth was going to have a baby in her old age. Mary hurried to help her, walking over the hills. When Mary said hello, Elizabeth's baby jumped for joy, because Jesus was inside Mary! Elizabeth said, “Blessed are you among women.” Mary stayed three months to help. We too can go quickly to help people in our family who need us.
family.intention: We pray for mothers who are expecting babies, and for grandparents and old people who need our help.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom can our family visit or help this week, like Mary helped Elizabeth?”

illus: A young woman from a village near Kottayam, expecting her first child, was living with her husband in Bengaluru when the doctor told her she must rest completely for the last three months. Her own mother had died years before. One evening her father's sister, a widow in her sixties from the hills of Idukki, rang to say she was coming. She arrived two days later after an overnight bus journey, with a cloth bag of jackfruit chips and a rosary, and stayed until the baby was baptised. She cooked, prayed the Rosary every evening at the young woman's bedside, and told stories of the family. Years later, when a neighbour in her building was in the same situation, the young mother went down every day to help. ‘My aunt never preached to me,’ she said. ‘She just came quickly, and stayed.’

pm.open: Holy Spirit, who filled Elizabeth at Mary's greeting, fill us now. With Mary, the Mother of our Lord, we gather to listen and to praise. Amen.
share: Mary set out and went with haste (Luke 1:39). What visit have I been postponing?
The child leaped in her womb (Luke 1:41). When has the nearness of Jesus filled me with joy?
Why has this happened to me, that the mother of my Lord comes to me? (Luke 1:43). How do I welcome Mary and Jesus into my home?
Blessed is she who believed (Luke 1:45). Which word of God do I find hard to believe?
pm.resp: Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us.
interc: For the Church, that like Mary she may go out in haste to carry Christ to all.
For expectant mothers and their unborn children, that they may be protected and welcomed with joy.
For the elderly and those who care for them, that no one may be left alone.
For families who prayed together in the month of Mary, that their prayer may continue through the year.
For all who doubt God's promises, that they may believe like Mary.
pm.close: Father, you made the Blessed Virgin Mary the dwelling of your Son and sent her in haste to serve. Through her intercession, give us faith in your word, joy in Christ's presence and genuine love for our neighbour. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today is the last day of the month of Mary, and the Church celebrates the Visitation. The angel has left Nazareth, the Son of God has taken flesh in Mary's womb, and Mary hears that Elizabeth, old and once barren, is expecting a child. What does she do? “Mary set out and went with haste” (Luke 1:39).

The first thing Mary does after receiving Jesus is to carry him to someone who needs her. Her haste is the haste of love and joy. In this Season of the Apostles, the Church does the same: whoever has received Christ goes out to bring him to others.

When Mary greets Elizabeth, the child in Elizabeth's womb leaps for joy, and Elizabeth is filled with the Holy Spirit. She cries out, “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb.” We say these words in every Hail Mary. And she calls Mary “the mother of my Lord” (Luke 1:43), the Mother of God.

Luke tells the story like the story of the ark of the covenant. David danced before the ark; John leaps before Jesus. The ark stayed three months in a house and brought blessing; Mary stays three months with Elizabeth. Mary is the new ark, the first tabernacle, carrying the living Bread to Elizabeth's home.

Elizabeth says, “blessed is she who believed” (Luke 1:45). Mary believed, and her faith became service. Saint Paul tells us how: let love be genuine, extend hospitality, rejoice with those who rejoice, weep with those who weep, associate with the lowly (Romans 12:9–16).

As we close the month of Mary, let us give her the gift she loves most: to believe God's word as she did, and to set out in haste to someone who needs us, carrying Jesus whom we have received in the Holy Qurbana. Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us. Amen.
kids: Children, Mary walked a long way over the hills to help her old cousin Elizabeth. When Mary said hello, baby John jumped for joy inside Elizabeth, because Jesus was there!
Like Mary, hurry to help someone this week: help Grandma, a little brother, or a friend. And every time you pray the Hail Mary, remember Elizabeth's happy words!
